Orthogonal norm preservation and Cauchy-Schwarz jointly produce the absolute cross-term bound. Both are necessary ingredients of the displayed source route, so their AND edge is genuine, not a flattening of alternative proofs.

The source kappa>=4 discharges nonnegativity of (kappa-1)/2. The lower and upper estimates consume opposite sides of the absolute cross-term estimate with that sign. No sign or cross-term estimate is promoted to a public hypothesis.

Symmetry is produced directly from the literal formula, independently of orthogonality. Symmetry, the two universal form bounds and the quadratic characterization jointly recover Loewner order. All four ingredients in the conclusion edge are justified; there is no alternative route in this source region requiring OR semantics.

The sealed signature has all orthogonal matrices, including both determinant components, and every real coordinate vector, including zero. It preserves n=3, kappa=4 and non-strict bounds. Its dot products represent the Euclidean quadratic form without invoking the Pi supremum norm. Ambient d and n<=d are not needed to state this bounded single-block intermediate result.
